messages:
alex: Hey, heads-up — noticing ~120 tiny GPU pods stuck Pending in apse1 across the warm-node pool. Scheduler says '0/8 nodes available' for a few of them even though prometheus shows free GPU capacity on multiple nodes.

sam: ugh. any taint/affinity denies in describe? can you paste `kubectl describe pod` for one?

alex: quick snippet from one describe: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason                  Age                 From               Message
  ----     ------                  ----                ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling        2m (x5 over 3m)     default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 7 node(s) didn't have available GPUs.
```

alex: but grafana shows 3 nodes with >0 GPUs free and `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable` is false.

jing: link to the warmpool heatmap? https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CP/warmpool?orgId=1 : I'm seeing a cluster of nodes in rack-r11 with NVLINK=isolated label set. those nodes have GPUs but are in a different NVLINK fabric partition — scheduler topology spread plugin might be rejecting them for these pods.

marco: are the pods requesting a specific topologySpreadConstraint or podAffinity? tiny pods should be tolerant.

alex: no, these are small inference pods (1 GPU, no affinity) — nothing explicit. they used to land fine. started after last night's rolling reboot of r11.

lina: devops-bot posted cordon events for r11 around 03:12 UTC during the reboot. maybe the cordon left a taint behind?

devops-bot: Node rack-r11-node-07 was cordoned by infra/maintenance at 2025-11-18T03:12:09Z and uncordoned at 2025-11-18T03:48:01Z. Patch applied: nvlink-firmware-1.2.4.

sam: can you check node labels/taints for those r11 nodes? commands: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l rack=r11 -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TAINTS:.spec.taints,LABELS:.metadata.labels
```

alex: ran it, output for node-07: `nvlink-partition=isolated`, taints: `gpu-reserve=true:NoSchedule`, but that taint is present on other racks too yet those accept pods.

jing: nvlink-partition label is new in our node-exporter after the firmware update — scheduler extender uses it for co-location to avoid cross-nvlink hops. Looks like the extender's compatibility matrix treats 'isolated' partitions as incompatible with the default model variant used by these pods.

marco: so scheduler thinks GPUs aren't "compatible" even though physically available. where is the compatibility policy defined? the runtime-config repo under infra/scheduler/policies has the mapping.

alex: checked infra/scheduler/policies/compat_matrix.yaml: there is an entry `inference-small: allowed_partitions: [full, shared]` — it does NOT include 'isolated'. That would explain it.

lina: why would that mapping change during a firmware rollout? was a policy update merged?

sam: anna merged a PR last week tightening compatibility to avoid slow NVLINK pairs for some jobs. maybe the new policy was deployed to apse1 accidentally with a different flag.

alex: action plan proposal: 1) temporarily include 'isolated' in allowed_partitions for inference-small in apse1 policy 2) trigger scheduler config reload 3) watch for perf regression (latency/kv hit rate).

jing: agree, can do a rolling change for apse1 only. Add a temporary flag `allow_isolated_fallback: true`. I'll open a PR and tag @sam for rollback guard.

sam: also run a one-off descheduler job to pull a few of the Pending pods into new nodes after policy change: `kubectl create job ... --image=descheduler:canary` — avoid mass churn.

marco: need telemetry baseline. alex, capture 5m avg p95/latency from inference-gateway and GPU utilization pre-change. post-change we'll compare.

alex: grabbing baseline now. p95 120ms -> 130ms on small traces, GPU util ~28% on the three isolated nodes.

devops-bot: PR #1422 opened: infra/scheduler/policies — temporarily add isolated partition to inference-small for apse1. Reviewer: sam.

lina: TY. once merged, remind infra to remove the flag after full validation or add an automatic 24h rollback.

jing: merged in canary, reloaded scheduler config on apse1-scheduler-0. waiting for cache sync.

alex: seeing pods start scheduling! 37 moved in the last 2m.

sam: descheduler job kicked to nudge remaining.

marco: watching perf dashboards — little/no regression so far. p95 dipped to 135ms briefly for the affected workers, back to 122ms.

alex: ok lemme run a guilt-check: do we accept 'isolated' long-term for this flavor?

sam: short-term we can allow it for inference-small with monitoring. long-term we need a better weight in compatibility matrix (prefer shared/full) and a scheduling score tweak instead of binary allow/deny.

jing: I'll file follow-up: instrument cross-partition slowdown, add score penalties rather than hard block, and plan a canary with 5% traffic.

lina: ops notes: remind oncall to watch eviction spikes after descheduler run and to keep an eye on rack-r11 thermal/firmware alerts — firmware might be causing odd NIC/conntrack flaps that we haven't surfaced yet.

alex: thanks all — closing this thread after we confirm the remaining 83 pods land and no regression for 1h.

devops-bot: Incident tracker updated: INC-2025-4912 — Temporary scheduler policy tweak applied to apse1; will auto-expire in 24h unless extended.

alex: closing — final status: 120 pending -> 0 pending, no SLO breach after 1h.
